description.value: Longitudinal resting-state fMRI study describing large-scale functional network abnormalities in unmedicated patients with schizophrenia and examining changes after six weeks of risperidone treatment.

spans.text: We collected resting state functional MRI data with a 3T scanner at baseline and six weeks after they were started on risperidone.

description.value: Longitudinal, non-randomized risperidone treatment study with baseline and six-week follow-up scans; healthy controls were scanned twice six weeks apart.

spans.text: Resting state scans were obtained prior to treatment (off medication) and after six weeks of treatment with risperidone.

spans.text: Subjects who were either medication naïve or had been off antipsychotic medications were enrolled in a six week trial with risperidone using a flexible dosing regimen.

value: In unmedicated SZ, we found increased functional connectivity in the DAN, ECN, and salience networks, but not the DMN when compared to HC.
DAN connectivity was increased in the angular gyrus, middle temporal gyrus, superior and inferior parietal gyri, cuneus/precuneus, superior and middle occipital gyrus, and calcarine sulcus.

value: We observed resting state functional connectivity changes after six weeks of treatment with risperidone only in the DAN, but none of the other networks.
Contrasting baseline and week six of treatment, an overall decrease in connectivity was seen in the lingual gyrus, fusiform gyrus, precuneus, calcarine sulcus and cerebellum.
